sentences.text: After due investigation, the police filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.

While according to the respondent no.1 claimed that the offending vehicle was not caused the accident and that the injuries sustained by the petitioner were not caused by the said vehicle, neither  SCCH-13 13 MVC.5733, 5734 &
 5735/2023 the driver nor the owner of the vehicle chose to challenge the charge sheet or resist the final report before the appropriate court.
 23.

Furthermore, respondent no.1 in an attempt to counter the direct testimony of the petitioners and the corroborating entries in the medical records and investigation report, has offered nothing beyond mere denials during the cross-examination of PW1 to PW3.
No cogent evidence has been produced to disprove the petitioners' version of events.

In the absence of any credible and substantive evidence to the contrary, this tribunal finds no merit in the assertion made by respondent no.1 that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the car and not on the part of the offending vehicle  24.
Furthermore, the petitioners have successfully established negligence through both oral and documentary evidence, which are consistent and corroborative.
On the other hand, no contra evidence has been placed on record to demonstrate that the driver of the offending vehicle was not negligent.
25 . By looking into the oral and documentary evidence it is clear that accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioners sustained injuries and damage sustained to the petitioners' car in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Liability:

Respondent No. 1-Insurance Company has specifically contended that the owner of the offending vehicle violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, inasmuch as the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a badge or a valid Driving Licence to drive a Goods vehicle at relevant point of time, the Insurance Company contends that it is not liable to indemnify the owner.

On this ground,
the insure claims to be absolved of any liability to pay compensation to the petitioners.
42. To support its contention, Investigation officer in Cr.131/2023, FDA, Jnanabharthi RTO, official of the respondent no 1, were examined as RW1 to RW3 respectively.

RW1 produced notice and reply notice at EX R1 and R2 and deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle did not hold an effective driving  SCCH-13 21 MVC.5733, 5734 &
 5735/2023 licence to drive the offending vehicle at relevant point of time.
RW2 has produced DL extract of one Murthy at EX R4, and stated that driver Murthy held a license to drive an LMV vehicle at relevant point of time.

However, the badge to drive a transport vehicle was obtained only on 16.4.2024 and is valid until 24.8.2038.
 43.
During the course cross-examination of RW2, it was brought on record that a person holding a licence for an LMV Vehicle is permitted to drive an unladen vehicle upto 3100 KG.
Respondent No. 1 examined its official as RW3, who deposed that the gross vehicle weight of the offending vehicle was 8,800. KGS.

Hence it is clear that the driver of the offending vehicle was not duly licensed to drive a transport vehicle of such capacity, thereby constitutes a breach of fundamental terms and conditions of the policy.
44 . RW1 relied upon the notice issued to the owner (Ex- R-1), and the reply received (Ex -R-2) from Respondent No.2, who is the owner of the offending vehicle.

In this reply, the owner failed to produce a  SCCH-13 22 MVC.5733, 5734 &
 5735/2023 valid DL, thereby supporting the insurance company's assertion.

45 . Furthermore, ExP-6 -Charge Sheet reveals that the driver was charge-sheeted under Section 279 and 338 IPC, read with Sections 181 and 180 of the Motor Vehicles Act, indicating that he did not hold a Manjula vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94448239/
12 valid or effective DL at relevant point of time, further strengthening the contention of the insurance company.

sentences.text: 46 . RW3 relied upon the insurance copy of offending vehicle at Ex.R6.
Which specifies that the Gross Vehicle Weight of the offending vehicle falls between 7501 -12000.
Ex. P6

clearly establishes that the offending vehicle was a heavy goods vehicle and the driver, not holding valid and effective badge to drive the offending vehicle at time of the accident, was unauthorised to drive it.

47 . It is also pertinent to note that Respondent No. 1, who is the owner of the offending vehicle, has neither contested the proceedings nor produced any rebuttal evidence either oral or documentary to  SCCH-13 23 MVC.5733, 5734 &
 5735/2023 establish that he held a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.

48 . In view of the unrebutted evidence on record,
this Tribunal holds that the offending vehicle was a heavy goods vehicle and the driver, not holding valid and effective badge to drive the offending vehicle at time of the accident, was unauthorised to drive it.
This clearly constitutes a willful breach of the terms and conditions of the policy contract.
49. In view of above discussion, the Respondent No.1 (Insurance Company) is not liable to indemnify the insured for the claim made under the present petition.

Consequently, Respondent No. 2, being the owner of the offending vehicle, is held liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and the liability to pay compensation rests solely with Respondent No.2, the owner of the offending vehicle.

MVC.5735/2023 ) vehicle in a road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The respondent denied all material averments in the petition and specifically denied that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Additionally, the offending vehicle had neither a valid permit nor a valid fitness certificate (FC) at the relevant time.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
No cogent evidence has been produced to disprove the petitioners' version of events.
In the absence of any credible and substantive evidence to the contrary, this tribunal finds no merit in the assertion made by respondent no.1 that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the car and not on the part of the offending vehicle  24.
Furthermore, the petitioners have successfully established negligence through both oral and documentary evidence, which are consistent and corroborative.
On the other hand, no contra evidence has been placed on record to demonstrate that the driver of the offending vehicle was not negligent.
25 . By looking into the oral and documentary evidence it is clear that accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioners sustained injuries and damage sustained to the petitioners' car in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
The petitioner has produced a medical bill at Ex.P.9, amounting to Rs.1,300/- which appear to be genuine upon scrutiny and that she was working at private as a Labour, earning Rs.16,000/- p.m.
, she has not produced any supporting documents to establish her avocation and income, nor has she adduced any evidence to prove that the injuries have resulted permanent disability or that she is unable to perform her work as earlier.
No medical expert has been examined to substantiate any claim of permanent disability.
28. There is also no cogent evidence to show that her injuries have affected her daily activities or caused long term functional impairment.
29. Considering the nature of the injury and in the absence of medical evidence specifically quantifying disability, this tribunal is of view that the petitioner must have endured considerable pain and suffering.
Taking into account her young age and the  SCCH-13 16 MVC.5733, 5734 &
 5735/2023 physical and emotional distress caused by the injury,
this court deems it appropriate to award global compensation of Rs.20,000/-.
Accordingly no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of education due to the accidental injuries.
40 . However, it has been clearly established that the damage to the petitioner's vehicle occurred due to the negligence of the respondent No.2.
Furthermore, it is not the case that the petitioner has received any compensation under the "Own Damage" claim from his insurance provider.
Accordingly, it is reasonable to  SCCH-13 20 MVC.5733, 5734 &
 5735/2023 infer that the petitioner would have incurred considerable expenses and inconvenience.
Respondent No. 1-Insurance Company has specifically contended that the owner of the offending vehicle violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, inasmuch as the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a badge or a valid Driving Licence to drive a Goods vehicle at relevant point of time, the Insurance Company contends that it is not liable to indemnify the owner.
Hence it is clear that the driver of the offending vehicle was not duly licensed to drive a transport vehicle of such capacity, thereby constitutes a breach of fundamental terms and conditions of the policy.
48 . In view of the unrebutted evidence on record,
this Tribunal holds that the offending vehicle was a heavy goods vehicle and the driver, not holding valid and effective badge to drive the offending vehicle at time of the accident, was unauthorised to drive it.
This clearly constitutes a willful breach of the terms and conditions of the policy contract.
49. In view of above discussion, the Respondent No.1 (Insurance Company) is not liable to indemnify the insured for the claim made under the present petition.
